newsitem.title: QATAR: Mideast Gulf oil product outlook - Soft, await IOC.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil product outlook - Soft, await IOC.

text.p: Gas oil and kerosene in the Mideast Gulf are likely to remain weighed down by unsold trader cargoes unless India Oil Corp's (IOC) May diesel tender beats market expectations, Gulf oil traders said on Thursday.
Gas oil cargoes were assessed at 40-45 cents premium to independent quotes though outright prices held up because of strong trade buying in the benchmark Singapore market, they said.
"Refiner supplies are quite tight but demand is fairly dead and there are cargoes in the hands of traders," said one Gulf-based executive.
Gas oil was assessed at $25.60 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday, a 40-cent spread to kerosene.

The next market momentum would come with IOC's diesel award though even here, Indian east coast demand would largely be met from Singapore while Gulf barrels would face tough competition from Mediterranean barrels for west India requirements.
IOC is expected to award its tender within 24 hours.
Gulf kerosene premiums were also seen pressured in a seasonal downturn with cargoes talked in a 30-35 cent premium range but had further downside potential, traders said.
Gasoline markets also lost trading momentum following an apparent decision by Saudi Aramco to delay buying spot cargoes for April, traders said.
"I wouldn't say Aramco has left the market. It didn't like the offers but that's not new...It will probably come back (to the market)," said one Gulf-based trader.
Fujairah bunker markets remained strong with 380-cst grade assessed at $96-98 a tonne.
